A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ART: Articulated Reconstruction Transformer. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and Appendices A–D are readable and support reliable comparison, including matching relocated implementation details.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction comparisons, component ablations, and qualitative results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 1, 4–7.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds runtime measurements in Table S1 and real-world reconstructions in Figure S1.

M1.justification: The part-slot transformer, hexa-plane representation, articulation prediction, rendering procedure, losses, and training stages are unchanged. Appendix D expands documentation without establishing a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: Figure S1 extends real-image evaluation beyond Figure 7's drawer example to four additional cases, including a bucket and kitchen appliances. Training data sources and the quantitative benchmark coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain URDFormer, SINGAPO, PARIS, DTA, and ArtGS in their respective comparisons. The added runtime table reuses these existing comparators without introducing or replacing a baseline.

E3.justification: Appendix A introduces runtime evaluation on a single A100 GPU, separately reporting monocular and multi-view ART. Existing benchmark splits, view/state counts, resolutions, and training budgets are unchanged; the new preprocessing description is disclosure rather than an established protocol revision.

E4.justification: The component ablations in Table 3 are unchanged. v3 adds four real-world case studies in Figure S1 and a qualitative, unquantified comparison of calibrated camera poses against optimizable view embeddings in Appendix D.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added runtime measurements are also reported as point estimates without uncertainty.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical scores. New Table S1 reports ART at 0.85 s multi-view and 0.42 s monocular, PARIS/DTA/ArtGS at 50/40/9 min, and URDFormer/SINGAPO at 2.37/0.54 s. Figure S1 adds four qualitative reconstructions; Appendix D additionally asserts better convergence and accuracy with calibrated poses without numerical results.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and parameterizations in Equations 1–6 and rendering derivations in Equations S1–S8 are unchanged apart from formatting and pagination. No new theorem, proof, or formal assumption is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about category-agnostic, feed-forward articulated reconstruction, joint part-level prediction, simulation-ready outputs, and superiority over existing baselines.

C2.justification: Appendix A newly attributes limited real-world texture reconstruction to the synthetic training domain. Appendix D expands the camera-pose rationale and explicitly describes single-object and segmentation-mask requirements. The main limitations concerning known part counts and calibrated poses remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly documents segmentation masks, square foreground-preserving cropping, and resizing for training and inference. Appendix A specifies runtime hardware and redirects supplementary-video instructions from index.html to the project webpage. Architecture and training details moved from Section 4 were already present in v1.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 71 references are unchanged. The added LRM-style implementation explanations do not substantively revise the contribution's positioning.

P1.justification: v3 adds limited explanatory prose to Appendices A and D, relocates the architecture/training-details paragraph from Section 4, and updates affiliation ordering and acknowledgments. The main narrative and section organization remain largely unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds runtime Table S1 and real-world Figure S1. It relocates the unchanged Figure 7 across columns and reflows surrounding text and appendix material; existing main figures and table structures are otherwise preserved.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly improves practical evidence and reproducibility through measured runtimes, broader real-world examples, and explicit input-preparation instructions. The new texture limitation also better qualifies applicability. These gains are limited: the central accuracy evidence is unchanged, and the added camera-pose comparison remains unquantified.
